Make batteries, lens protection and the correct manual available to the person who uses the camera. thermal thermals thermal camera NETD infrared camera Choose observation or measurement deliberately Compare purchase support and repeatability Define the job Distinguish outdoor observation from building inspection or calibrated temperature measurement. These require different capabilities. Separate sensor and screen claims Check native thermal sensor resolution, field of view, sensitivity and whether the device supports temperature measurement. Recognize image limits Ordinary glass, reflective surfaces, weather and obstructions affect interpretation. A bright patch alone does not identify its cause. Confirm before acting Use qualified help for electrical, structural or medical concerns. Do not open hazardous equipment to investigate an interesting image.

title: Thunderstorm
summary: Go inside a substantial building or a fully enclosed hard-top vehicle when thunder is heard. Stay away from windows and monitor warnings for damaging wind, hail, tornadoes and flash flooding.
text: Check for downed lines and flooded routes before travel. Schedule outdoor work around forecasts. Every thunderstorm can produce lightning, even without a severe thunderstorm warning. Use a substantial building or enclosed hard-top vehicle even when warnings cannot be checked. Avoid plumbing and wired electrical equipment during lightning. Watch for rising water and damaging wind without going outside to observe the storm. Account for children, older people, pets and anyone who needs assistance before moving. Keep shoes, medicines and a torch in the shelter area. Decide who helps whom and who carries the essential supplies; do not send a lone child to retrieve items. For this situation, brief every person on the first action: get indoors. Agree who will manage children, pets or mobility needs while that action happens. Every thunderstorm can produce lightning, even without a severe thunderstorm warning. Severe storms Get indoors Open shelters, tents and trees do not protect from lightning. Avoid conductive paths Inside, avoid plumbing and plugged-in equipment during lightning. Read new warnings Move to an interior room for severe wind or hail; use a tornado shelter if a tornado warning is issued. Wait before returning After the last thunder, wait at least 30 minutes before resuming outdoor activity.

title: Tornado
summary: If a tornado warning covers your location, shelter now in a basement or small interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. Stay away from windows and cover your head and neck. A mobile home is not a safe tornado shelter.
text: What if there is no basement? Identify an interior room on the lowest usable floor of a substantial building, away from windows. Plan the shortest route there before a warning. Protect the head and neck with available protection; equipment retrieval must not delay shelter. What if I am in a mobile home? A mobile home is not a tornado shelter even when tied down. Arrange a nearby substantial shelter before storms arrive and move while there is safe time. Do not wait for visible damage to decide that a different location is needed.  Afterward, avoid damaged buildings, broken glass and downed lines. Check for injuries and use text to let your contact know you are safe. Do not wait to see a funnel. Darkness and rain can hide tornadoes. A watch calls for readiness; a warning calls for action. Go to your identified shelter without waiting for confirmation when a warning or nearby clear danger is present. Keep shoes, a light and head protection close. If in a mobile home, use a nearby sturdy shelter before conditions worsen; never attempt to outrun a tornado in traffic. Choose a shelter that can actually fit and be reached by everyone. Keep shoes, a light and necessary mobility aids nearby; supervise children and secure pets without blocking the route. Rehearse how a person who cannot hear warnings will be notified. Severe storms Go to the shelter Move immediately; put shoes on if within reach and take your phone without delaying. Use a designated storm shelter when accessible. Protect your head Crouch low and cover your head and neck with your arms. Use a sturdy table or available cushioning for additional protection. If outside or in a vehicle Get to a nearby sturdy building if safely possible. Do not shelter under an overpass. Vehicles and mobile homes offer little protection. Keep listening Use local warning messages or weather radio; remain sheltered until the threat has passed and official updates permit leaving.

title: Trailer, RV and mobile-home preparedness
summary: Plan early access to a sturdy shelter and a safe destination. A trailer, RV or mobile home is not a safe tornado shelter; supplies and tie-downs do not change that limitation.
text: Can tie-downs make a mobile home safe in a tornado? No. Use the appropriate sturdy shelter plan. Property reinforcement does not remove the need for a safe place for people. Do we have to take the RV or trailer when leaving? No. Have a people-only departure plan for when moving the unit is unsafe, impractical or would delay required evacuation. Identify the unit and the limit that supplies cannot fix A manufactured home, motorhome and towable travel trailer have different movement, structural and utility arrangements. Write what the actual unit is, how it is occupied and whether it can legally and practically move. A mobile home may not be movable in an emergency. A vehicle-based unit may still need considerable preparation and a suitable driver. Do not let the word mobile substitute for a transport plan. A trailer or mobile home is not a safe tornado shelter NWS directs people in mobile homes to sturdy shelter. Identify and use an appropriate shelter plan before travel becomes dangerous; tie-downs, supplies and a reinforced storage bin do not remove this limitation. For other severe wind threats, use the applicable local evacuation and housing guidance. Florida’s manufactured-home guidance emphasizes early planning, qualified assessment of anchors and attachments, and departure arrangements. Its rules and programs are a Florida example, not a universal building standard. Property preparations and decisions about where people shelter are separate tasks. Confirm a sturdy destination and how people reach it Identify an appropriate destination before a watch or warning leaves little time. Check access, availability, transport time, pets and essential care. A clubhouse or campground office is not proven shelter merely because it looks more substantial than the trailer. Ask the responsible operator or local emergency management what the site actually provides and under which conditions it opens. Keep the people plan ahead of the unit plan Forecast preparation Review warnings, transport, destination access and care needs early. Departure decision Use applicable instructions and the household trigger while safe travel remains possible. People first Leave the unit when necessary; do not wait for towing or property work to be completed. Editorial planning aid. Actual hazards, individual needs and current instructions control the response. Time an ordinary safe journey with the actual household and discuss what changes if the usual driver is away. Keep an alternate appropriate site where possible. Record the exact address and entry arrangement on paper. A destination that requires a locked gate, an absent manager or inaccessible steps needs a solution in advance. Do not plan last-minute driving through a storm as the default. Separate relocation of people from moving the whole unit Moving an RV or trailer involves more than starting a vehicle. The manufacturer’s travel procedure, loading, connections, vehicle condition, towing capability and route restrictions all matter. Plan those tasks in normal conditions and use qualified help for technical questions. During a developing hazard, determine whether there is enough safe time for that actual sequence. Possessions should not delay the household’s necessary departure. Two distinct departure checklists People leave The unit moves only when safe and suitable Account for people and pets. Use the manufacturer’s travel and towing procedure. Take essential care and manageable portable items. Verify vehicle condition and appropriate load limits. Use a checked destination and safe route. Check the route and destination can accommodate the unit. Notify the household contact when safe. Arrange an experienced suitable driver and necessary preparation. If moving the unit is no longer appropriate, use the leave-the-unit plan. Do not attempt repairs, hookup, fuel transfer or salvage in dangerous conditions. A road reachable by a passenger car may not be suitable for a large rig. Avoid assuming that a map’s shortest route accounts for clearances, weight or towing constraints. Maintain installed systems through model-specific instructions Keep manuals and qualified service contacts for the unit’s electrical, battery, propane, heating, ventilation, water and alarm systems. Inspect and maintain them according to their instructions. Use safe compatible supplies and appropriate professional help for faults. A household preparedness guide cannot replace the wiring or fuel-system documentation for a particular model. Keep exits, hatches and necessary ventilation clear of supplies. Know the documented response to a suspected fuel leak; leave danger and contact the appropriate service from safety. Check alarms through their specified test and replacement process. Plan safe water and sanitation around actual tank or service limitations; a gauge is not a water-quality test. Keep fuel-burning equipment and generator exhaust out of the unit and neighboring occupied spaces. Do not improvise adapters, electrical backfeeding, or indoor combustion because an outage interrupts normal comfort. Before a season of use, check whether another adult can find the manuals and explain the stop conditions. Separate ordinary travel procedures from emergency response. Shutting down or reconnecting equipment during an unsafe event should follow the applicable professional or manufacturer instructions, not a universal online sequence. Generator safety Safe water reserves Store a useful reserve without blocking movement or overloading Compact living makes storage, weight and access part of preparedness. Record safe storage locations for suitable water, meals, lights, care supplies and documents. Observe the actual unit and vehicle limits using manufacturer information and appropriate assessment. Water and batteries can add substantial weight; do not assume unused cabinet space means unlimited load capacity. A compact storage review Area Question Door or hatch Can the full escape route open without moving boxes? Care supplies Can the right person reach them without unsafe lifting? Water and food Are storage conditions, containers and handling suitable? Travel items Are they secured appropriately for ordinary movement? title: Tropical storm
summary: Treat tropical storm warnings seriously: dangerous flooding, surge, wind and tornadoes can occur. Check local evacuation instructions, avoid flooded roads, and take shelter before conditions become unsafe.
text: Monitor updates after the storm passes; rivers may keep rising and power lines may remain live. A storm below hurricane strength can still cause catastrophic flooding. Prepare for loss of water, electricity and communications even if the storm is not a hurricane. Move out of flood and surge areas before access is lost. Do not use the storm name or wind category as proof that your route or home is safe. Account for children, older people, pets and anyone who needs assistance before moving. Keep shoes, medicines and a torch in the shelter area. Decide who helps whom and who carries the essential supplies; do not send a lone child to retrieve items. For this situation, brief every person on the first action: read all warnings. Agree who will manage children, pets or mobility needs while that action happens. A storm below hurricane strength can still cause catastrophic flooding. Tropical weather Read all warnings Check flood, surge and tornado notices as well as wind forecasts. Prepare before arrival Charge devices, secure loose outdoor items while safe and arrange essential medicines and supplies. Leave if ordered Follow the evacuation zone and route instructions for your address. Keep travel limited Stay off roads during hazardous weather and never drive into floodwater.

title: Tsunami
summary: Near the coast, strong or long shaking, a sudden unusual sea rise or retreat, or a loud ocean roar can signal a tsunami. After shaking stops, move to high ground and inland immediately. Do not wait for an official warning when natural warning signs are present.
text: Know coastal evacuation routes before visiting. Use designated vertical evacuation structures where local plans provide them. The first wave may not be largest. Dangerous currents can last for hours. Use natural warning signs to move inland and uphill immediately after shaking. Walk if roads are jammed and a safe pedestrian route is available. Stay away from the shore through later waves; quiet water or lack of a broadcast is not an all-clear. Account for children, older people, pets and anyone who needs assistance before moving. Keep shoes, medicines and a torch in the shelter area. Decide who helps whom and who carries the essential supplies; do not send a lone child to retrieve items. For this situation, brief every person on the first action: protect during shaking. Agree who will manage children, pets or mobility needs while that action happens. Wait for clearance Stay out of the evacuation zone until authorities say it is safe.

title: Understanding your firearm: parts, actions and maintenance
summary: Understand the exact model as an ownership system: action, chamber designation, fit, documentation and routine care. Use its official manual to distinguish owner maintenance from service work, and compare the complete equipment cost before adding accessories.
text: The major parts and what their names mean A sporting rifle: external parts vocabulary Conceptual sporting-rifle outline showing stock, receiver/action, barrel, muzzle and magazine. The chamber is at the rear of the barrel. Actual shapes and controls vary; this is not an operating or assembly diagram. A component glossary Term Function or location Barrel / bore The barrel is the tube; the bore is its interior passage. Rifling consists of spiral features inside a rifled bore. Muzzle The forward opening of the barrel. Chamber The cartridge-holding portion at the rear of the barrel; revolvers have chambers in the cylinder. Receiver / frame The main structure supporting relevant mechanisms; naming varies by firearm type. Action The mechanism associated with loading, closing, firing and removing a cartridge case. Magazine A cartridge supply, fixed or detachable depending on the firearm. It is not the chamber. Stock / grip The parts held or supported by the user; shape and fit affect comfort. These terms make manuals, service discussions and product descriptions easier to understand. A clip is not simply another name for every magazine. A sporting rifle drawing also does not map directly onto a revolver or shotgun. Use the parts list supplied with the exact model to identify controls and components rather than assuming their positions from a generic diagram. Action types: what the category actually describes Common sporting action families Type General mechanical distinction Bolt action A bolt is manually operated as part of the loading and extraction cycle. Lever action A lever operates the action; cartridge storage and other details vary by design. Pump action A sliding fore-end operates the action; common in sporting shotguns and some rifles. Break action The firearm opens at a hinge to expose its chamber or chambers. Revolver A rotating cylinder contains multiple chambers. Semiautomatic Energy from a shot cycles the action; one shot is fired for each trigger actuation. Semiautomatic does not mean fully automatic. Single-action and double-action are another classification: they describe what a trigger actuation does in relation to preparing and releasing the firing mechanism. They do not tell you whether the firearm uses a detachable magazine, how its manual safety works or which cartridge it accepts. Striker-fired and hammer-fired describe different firing-mechanism arrangements, not universal quality rankings. An action type can help explain why two firearms have different controls and maintenance requirements, but the exact design matters. Two semiautomatic sporting rifles can have different operating systems, while two revolvers can require different handling practices. Familiarity with a category is useful background; it does not replace learning a particular model. Chamber, magazine and controls: avoid the common assumptions A cartridge can remain in a chamber independently of what is in the magazine. That is why removing a detachable magazine alone is not an unloaded-condition check. A visible indicator or an apparently open action is also not a substitute for the manufacturer’s complete verification procedure. Learn that procedure in a suitable setting with competent instruction, rather than improvising from a diagram. Mechanical safeties differ. Some block or disconnect parts of the firing mechanism; some designs have several passive features; some lack an external safety lever. A safety’s presence does not establish that every possible impact or handling error is harmless. A decocker is not simply another name for a safety, and its operation must be learned from the exact manual. Do not infer loaded condition from the magazine, a lever position or a sound. Identify the chamber marking separately from a model name stamped elsewhere. Check whether a manual covers your exact variant and revision. Recognize that older examples and modified firearms may not match a current marketing description. Good terminology prevents costly confusion when contacting support. Saying “the magazine release is damaged” is more useful than “the button is wrong,” while reporting the model and variant helps the manufacturer identify the relevant controls. Keep a clear photograph of markings in your private equipment record. Routine care: cleaning is not the same as repair Routine maintenance preserves condition; it should follow the manufacturer’s instructions for the exact firearm. Different finishes, materials and mechanisms can require different products. More solvent, more oil or more disassembly does not automatically improve the result. Excess products can attract contamination or reach places the manual says to keep dry. Keep the maintenance boundary clear Task Useful approach Routine exterior care Follow the manual’s approved products and protection instructions. Scheduled cleaning Use the manufacturer’s procedure and limits; do not substitute an unrelated model’s tutorial. Parts replacement Confirm whether this is an owner-permitted task or qualified service work. Abnormal operation Stop use and arrange appropriate assessment; cleaning is not a universal fault repair. Unknown modifications Establish what was changed before relying on an old manual or standard parts list. Keep live ammunition out of the maintenance area and establish the unloaded condition using the exact instructions before beginning. Use a clear workspace and keep cleaning chemicals away from food and children. Record the date, products used and any concern discovered. A short log supports warranty service and reveals a recurring issue that might otherwise be forgotten. Do not file, bend or adjust firing-mechanism parts to resolve an unexplained symptom. Ordinary care and altering mechanical behavior are different jobs. If a manufacturer notice describes a recall or safety bulletin, follow it even if the firearm seems to operate normally. Wear, obstruction and disaster exposure Pay attention to changes: visible damage, newly loose components, unusual operation, unexplained corrosion or a different report during sporting use. An obstruction in the bore can be hazardous. If something suggests a blockage or mechanical fault, stop using the firearm and follow the manufacturer’s assessment process; do not try another shot to determine whether the concern was real. A firearm exposed to floodwater or fire needs a different decision from a routine post-range cleaning. Water can reach concealed mechanisms, and heat can affect materials without an obvious exterior change. Secure the equipment and arrange qualified inspection under the relevant manufacturer and SAAMI guidance. Photograph its identification and record the event from a safe location. Secondhand equipment deserves an especially clear baseline. Obtain the manual, check manufacturer notices and establish its condition and modification history before use. A seller’s statement that it “worked last time” does not document present condition. A qualified inspection can be more valuable than immediately buying accessories for an unfamiliar firearm. A concise safety foundation that supports better learning Keep the muzzle in a direction that would not injure someone if the firearm discharged. Keep fingers outside the trigger guard until the appropriate point in a lawful sporting activity. Identify the target and what lies beyond it, use an appropriate range or hunting setting, and wear suitable eye and hearing protection. Mechanical features support these practices; they do not replace them. Separate handling from alcohol, impairment, fatigue and interruptions. Secure firearms against unauthorized access and account for children, visitors and changes in household risk. Anyone who finds an unfamiliar firearm should leave it alone, move away and tell a responsible adult. Safety education for children supplements adult storage responsibility. For your next learning session, choose a specific question: identifying controls on your model, understanding its authorized routine care or interpreting a safety bulletin. Work with the manual and qualified instruction for hands-on learning. A focused question creates progress; a vague claim of being “experienced with guns” can leave important model-specific gaps unnoticed. Turn the parts list into an ownership file Knowing component names becomes more useful when they connect to a particular rifle. Keep a short record with the model, complete chamber designation, manual edition, stock configuration as supplied, included accessories and support contact. Store serial numbers and purchase records privately; the bag label or public photograph does not need that information. For a used firearm, record which items are documented and which require clarification. A model-specific care record Field Useful entry Manual Exact model family, revision and where the relevant care section begins. Consumables Manufacturer-approved cleaning products and the surfaces each is intended for. Routine observations Date, weather/storage exposure, visible condition and care performed. Service question Observed symptom, when it appeared and any manufacturer response. Photograph ordinary external condition for your private records without trying to diagnose internal faults from an image. A dated note such as “returned wet from transport; care completed according to manual” is more informative than “cleaned.” Keep service receipts with that record so a future owner or technician can distinguish observation from work actually performed. Cleaning is a product-specific workflow A useful maintenance plan names the work area, compatible products, owner-authorized tasks and how the equipment returns to storage. Start with the manual’s maintenance section and product labels. Keep the instructions available while working; a video for a visually similar model may refer to a different mechanism or revision. This overview does not provide disassembly, adjustment, tuning or repair instructions. Organize a care session Identify Confirm the model and applicable manual; list the tasks the owner is permitted to perform. Prepare Provide good light, ventilation appropriate to the product labels, a stable workspace and separate storage for ammunition. Document Record the work and observations, account for the equipment, and follow the manual’s return-to-storage requirements. Osprey Zero planning aid. These are conditional choices; current conditions and individual needs control the decision. Buy cleaning equipment around the manual rather than a large universal kit. Consider which materials are compatible with finishes, which consumables can be replenished locally, and whether the included instructions are understandable. A maintenance log also supports decisions about recurring consumable cost and professional service. Do not establish a universal schedule such as a fixed number of shots: exposure, storage and model requirements differ. Ruger · Official instruction manual finder Find the manual for the exact model; read the maintenance and service boundaries before buying a cleaning kit. Two current manufacturer examples show why the exact version matters: Ruger publishes a separate American Rifle Generation II manual and a 10/22 Standard manual limited to model numbers 32000 and higher. Use the finder for another version. Read the relevant maintenance and service sections for the actual model rather than transferring a procedure between these examples. Ruger · American Rifle Generation II manual Official Generation II manual, revision 3/2026 R4. Match the exact firearm and use the manufacturer’s owner-care and service sections. Ruger · 10/22 Standard manual: models 32000 and higher Official 6/2026 R1 manual for this model-number range. Other 10/22 versions use different manuals; resolve them with the official finder. Choose one model-specific question and find its answer in the manual or through qualified instruction. Start with controls, loaded-condition verification or routine care. Damage, suspected bore obstruction, abnormal operation, a manufacturer safety notice and flood or fire exposure require a pause and appropriate assessment. Do not continue sporting use to “see if it happens again.” Keep the firearm secured and unused while you identify it and obtain its manual or inspection. Do not substitute a similar-looking model’s instructions or attempt a repair to make unfamiliar equipment usable. Limit access to authorized adults who understand the exact firearm and storage system. Review access after visitors, a move, memory changes or a household crisis; familiarity never replaces secure storage. Safe ownership guns weapons gun safety Turn the parts list into an ownership file Cleaning is a product-specific workflow Make a model record Record the exact model and chamber designation, manual revision, acquisition information and manufacturer support route. Choose a useful ownership context List your sporting or range requirements, transport, storage, fit and annual cost. Plan routine care Use the exact manual to select compatible cleaning products, permitted owner tasks and inspection intervals. Keep service records Record care, unusual wear, storage exposure and manufacturer advice; service questions belong with the manufacturer or qualified professional.

title: Using an AED
summary: For an unresponsive person who is not breathing normally, call emergency services and begin CPR. Turn on the AED as soon as it arrives and follow its voice and picture prompts. Do not touch the person during rhythm analysis or a shock.
text: Keep the AED connected until responders take over. Learn the location of nearby devices and obtain training. For a child or infant, use the appropriate pediatric pads or setting when available and follow the device and dispatcher instructions. If nobody can bring an AED, continue CPR rather than leaving the person to search alone. If another person is present, ask them to locate the nearest accessible AED while you continue compressions. Follow the device prompts when it arrives. Give someone the specific task of calling or locating care while another person provides first aid. Keep the patient warm or cool as the condition requires and record what happened and when. Do not put yourself into the same hazard or assume an ambulance has been dispatched until confirmed. For this situation, brief every person on the first action: turn it on. Agree who will manage children, pets or mobility needs while that action happens. For a child or infant, use the appropriate pediatric pads or setting when available and follow the device and dispatcher instructions. Resuscitation Turn it on Continue CPR while another helper prepares the AED if possible. Expose the chest Dry a wet chest and place pads according to the AED diagrams. title: Vehicle breakdown
summary: Move out of traffic if you safely can, switch on hazard lights and call roadside assistance or emergency services for immediate danger. Give your road, direction and nearest marker. On a high-speed road, follow local road-authority advice about whether to stay belted inside or exit to a protected area.
text: Carry water, weather protection, a charged phone and a vehicle kit. Check tires, fuel or charge before travel. Exit choices depend on the road and surroundings; do not apply one universal rule to every breakdown. Record your exact location, stay visible without standing in traffic and conserve your phone. Do not begin walking along a dangerous road or into remote terrain without a known reachable refuge. In heat or cold, watch occupants closely and reassess whether the vehicle remains safe. Count occupants, monitor temperature and keep children away from traffic. Preserve medicines, water and a light within reach. Do not split the group without a clear safe destination and a reliable way to reconnect. For this situation, brief every person on the first action: protect from traffic. Agree who will manage children, pets or mobility needs while that action happens. Exit choices depend on the road and surroundings; do not apply one universal rule to every breakdown. Roadside Protect from traffic Do not stand in travel lanes or between vehicles. Avoid repairs beside moving traffic. Assess immediate danger If fire, smoke or a collision threat makes the vehicle unsafe, move to a safe location away from traffic when possible. Wait safely Keep children and pets protected and conserve phone power. In remote areas do not wander without a known safe destination.

title: Vehicle emergency kit: useful supplies, safe access
summary: Pack for the passengers and climate, keep essentials reachable, and service the vehicle before relying on it. A repair tool is useful only where you can use it safely.
text: Should I carry jumper cables? Only if appropriate for your vehicle and you know its exact procedure. Some vehicles have designated connection points or restrictions. Check the manual; do not improvise with an unfamiliar high-voltage or damaged battery. A practical starter shopping list Editorial starting point: flashlight with suitable spare batteries, phone cable and compatible charger, reflective vest, work gloves, drinking water, ready-to-eat snacks, weather layers, paper map and a basic first-aid kit. Then add vehicle-specific tools. Avoid buying a large prepacked kit before checking whether its contents suit your climate and passengers. Rotate for the season Review food, water containers and batteries after prolonged heat or freezing conditions. Follow product storage instructions. Add winter clothing for cold routes and check cooling-system maintenance for hot routes. A medicine left in a hot trunk may no longer meet its storage requirements; ask a pharmacist about a suitable travel arrangement. Unpack your current car kit, remove unusable items and practice finding the light and contacts without turning on cabin lights. Never leave children or pets in a hot parked vehicle. Never run an engine in an enclosed space. Flooded roads, wires and active traffic can make staying or repairing unsafe. If help cannot be reached, assess exposure and traffic before attempting any repair. Keep the group together in the safest available location and conserve phone power. Do not turn a mechanical problem into a traffic injury. Pack for children, pets and anyone who cannot comfortably wait outdoors. Keep communication aids and mobility equipment accessible. A lone driver should know where the kit is without searching the trunk in darkness. car kit roadside supplies trunk kit Start with people Carry drinking water, familiar shelf-stable food, layers, a flashlight, first-aid supplies and a phone charging cable. Add medicines and passenger-specific essentials within their storage limits. Check the vehicle Check tires, lights and fluids against the owner’s manual. Use the vehicle’s recommended tire pressure, not the maximum printed on the tire. Inspect the spare if fitted. Match tools to your car Confirm that the jack, spare, tire tool or repair kit actually fits. Learn the manufacturer’s procedure in a safe practice setting. Roadside assistance is a backup, not a reason to work beside moving traffic. Organize access Keep a light, phone and contact details accessible from the cabin. title: Verify emergency information
summary: Check the source, time, exact location and evidence before acting on or sharing an emergency message. Compare independent sources when possible. A forwarded screenshot, logo or urgent voice note is not verification. Act on obvious immediate danger without waiting for a post to be confirmed.
text: Check the source, time, exact location and evidence before acting on or sharing an emergency message. Compare independent sources when possible. Keep a short list of known sources saved offline, including non-government humanitarian sources. Choose information based on reliability and relevance, not simply whether it is official or unofficial. Verification should not delay escape from visible fire, rising water or another immediate hazard. No source can guarantee that conditions remain unchanged. If connectivity fails, use the observations you can obtain safely and your written plans. Do not travel into danger to confirm a rumour or follow a single anonymous message. Assign a trusted adult to each person who needs assistance. Keep medicines, essential contacts and a workable reunion plan with the group. title: Volcanic eruption
summary: Follow the local volcano evacuation order and stay out of restricted zones. If ash is falling and you are not told to evacuate, stay indoors with windows and doors closed. Avoid river valleys where volcanic mudflows may travel.
text: Wait for reentry instructions. Do not climb a roof covered in ash; wet ash can overload structures. A particle respirator does not protect against volcanic gases. Keep away from river valleys, exclusion areas and visible ash plumes. Use the best reachable intact shelter for ashfall while checking evacuation information. Avoid driving through heavy ash unless leaving a more immediate threat; ash can impair engines and visibility. Account for children, older people, pets and anyone who needs assistance before moving. Keep shoes, medicines and a torch in the shelter area. Decide who helps whom and who carries the essential supplies; do not send a lone child to retrieve items. Limit ash exposure Close outside-air openings and use eye protection and a well-fitting particulate respirator for necessary outdoor movement. Keep roads clear Avoid driving in ash unless necessary; visibility and engines can be affected.

title: Water disruption
summary: After a water outage, damaged pipes or suspected contamination, use sealed bottled or previously stored safe water until you establish the risk. Boil-water, do-not-drink and do-not-use notices mean different things. Boiling kills germs but does not remove fuel, chemicals or radioactive contamination. If notices are unavailable, do not treat clear water or restored pressure as proof of safety.
text: Read the exact notice before treating or using tap water.  What does the notice actually restrict? Read its name and affected area: boil-water, do-not-drink and do-not-use notices have different consequences. If the reason is unknown, do not assume a filter or boiling resolves it. Use a verified alternate drinking source while checking the restriction. Someone already drank suspect water — now what? Record the source and time and seek medical or poison guidance when reachable, especially after a chemical warning or new symptoms. Do not induce vomiting or give an improvised treatment. Severe symptoms need urgent care rather than a water-treatment tutorial.  Store water and a printed copy of your utility's alert channel. Know whether anyone in the household needs extra water or cannot use a typical treatment method. Do not boil water suspected of chemical or fuel contamination. Boiling can concentrate some contaminants; use the alternative source named in the notice. If there is no notice after pressure loss, flooding or damaged pipes, use sealed or previously stored safe water while you establish the risk. Do not assume that boiling solves an unknown contamination problem. Label containers and keep drinking water separate from cleaning water. Include drinking, medicines, infant feeding and food preparation in the safe-water plan. Tell every caregiver which container is clean and which tap uses are restricted. Consider people who cannot read the warning or lift a large container. Water Identify the notice Find the utility or health department notice for your address, its start time, reason, and permitted uses. Save a screenshot in case service fails. Match use to the instruction A boil-water notice generally addresses microbes; follow the authority's boil directions. If the notice says do not drink or do not use, follow those stricter limits and the specified alternative-water instructions. Protect priority needs Set aside approved water for drinking, infant formula, medications, tooth brushing, food preparation, and pets, as the notice directs. Wait for clearance Do not assume that water is safe because it looks clear or service has returned. Follow flushing or filter replacement instructions after an official all-clear.

title: Water outage
summary: Check the utility notice to learn whether water service is interrupted and whether an advisory applies. Use stored or commercially bottled water for drinking and essential care. Service returning does not automatically mean tap water is safe.
text: Can stored water serve every task? Separate drinking and food-preparation water from water for cleaning or flushing. Keep clean containers covered and labeled. A source suitable for a toilet is not necessarily safe for hands, utensils or drinking. What changes when pressure returns? Find the utility’s actual notice. Returning flow does not by itself establish drinking safety after a pressure loss. Use the relevant boil-water, do-not-drink or do-not-use guide and check whether the notice has been lifted. Identify the problem before using another source A dry tap, low pressure, visibly unusual water, and a formal water advisory are different situations. Start by checking a reliable utility or public-health notice when reachable. Record the affected area, time, exact restrictions, and where updates will appear. For a private well, a power failure or flood may require a different response from a municipal main break. Read the advisory: three different decisions Boil water Follow the notice’s microbial-risk instructions for relevant uses. An ordinary pitcher filter does not cancel the advisory. Do not drink Use the specified safe alternative for drinking and food. Boiling does not make harmful chemicals or toxins safe. Do not use Avoid tap-water contact and uses covered by the notice. Use the directed alternative; do not substitute a boil routine. The exact local advisory controls. This diagram explains the labels; it does not certify a particular supply. If information cannot be obtained, avoid treating water of uncertain quality as confirmed drinking water. Use known-safe stored or commercially bottled water for essential consumption and make a plan to obtain more. Water looking clear or pressure returning does not establish that it is safe. Keep drinking-quality water for the right tasks Common uses to check during an advisory Task Practical question Drinking and medicines Is the water confirmed suitable to swallow? Food preparation and brushing teeth Could water be ingested, even in a small amount? Ice and refrigerator dispensers Are these connected to the affected supply? Stop using them during an advisory. Infant feeding What suitable ready-to-use or provider-directed option is available? Pets Are they receiving the safe alternative required by the notice? Bathing, handwashing, and laundry What does this specific advisory allow? Do not infer permissions from another type of notice. Tell every household member about the restriction, including visitors and anyone who might make a drink from habit. Put a clear notice at the affected taps. If a person cannot read the notice or needs support with routines, arrange direct assistance rather than relying on a label alone. Keep the source and date with any new water brought home. A reused bottle from an unknown supply is not equivalent to unopened commercial water. Separate food preparation from the collection and handling of uncertain water so containers cannot easily be mixed up. Calculate what you have and when you need more Count only confirmed drinking-quality water. Write the amount in one unit so bottles labelled in litres and jugs labelled in gallons do not cause a counting error. Record people, pets, care requirements, and the amount already used. The emergency storage baseline is a starting point; actual household needs may be greater. An editorial example: three people with nine gallons of safe water have three days at one gallon per person per day before extra needs. If measured use is four gallons a day, the same reserve is about two and a quarter days. Use the shorter realistic estimate to arrange supply early. Do not ration necessary drinking water to stretch the spreadsheet. Choose the next source before the reserve is nearly empty. Check whether the source is suitable, open, reachable, and able to provide the amount you need. Choose containers and transport the household can actually manage. Preserve some ready-to-carry water if a move becomes necessary. Emergency water storage quantities Handle a boil-water notice correctly Use commercially bottled water when available, or follow the local boil instructions. CDC’s general microbial-risk method is a full rolling boil for one minute, or three minutes above 6,500 feet, then allow the water to cool before use. The notice may give additional directions for the local situation. Boil tap water as required even if it has passed through a normal home filter. Plan the process before heating: suitable water source, permitted cooking method, stable pot, safe cooling location, clean storage container, and a person who can carry it safely. Keep children away from the hot-water area. Do not make an unsafe indoor use of outdoor cooking equipment part of the treatment plan. Boiling has a defined purpose This method addresses germs. It does not remove harmful chemical contamination or make a do-not-use supply acceptable. If the advisory is not microbial, switch to the specified alternative water. Make only the amount you can cool, store, and dispense cleanly. Mark the container and prevent someone from refilling it from the restricted tap. If you lack a safe way to heat and handle water, prioritize an approved alternative supply instead of improvising. Manage hygiene and toilet needs separately A water outage is also a hygiene problem. Work out where people can wash hands, how meals can be prepared without contaminating them, and what toilet arrangement is usable. Do not count all available water as suitable for every purpose. A do-not-use notice can prohibit skin contact as well as drinking. Read the actual permission for handwashing and bathing in the notice. Advice for a boil-water event does not automatically apply to a chemical event. Keep a small, clearly identified handwashing station with suitable water where food is prepared and near toilet arrangements. Reduce unnecessary water-heavy chores while preserving essential hygiene and care. Check whether wastewater service is functioning before adding water to toilets or drains, especially when there is a sewer warning or backup. Bath water collected before a disruption is not automatically drinking water. Label water reserved for an allowed non-drinking task and keep its containers separate. If sewage backs up, isolate the affected area and follow the sewer-failure guidance; repeated flushing can worsen the situation. Sewer failure Emergency hygiene Resupply without turning the trip into another problem Confirm a distribution point or retailer before travelling when possible. Ask what containers are needed, what water is supplied, and whether there are quantity limits or access needs. The source may be appropriate for only certain uses; retain any instructions given with it. A collection plan for the household Step What to decide Quantity How much confirmed safe water is needed before the next realistic supply opportunity? Carrying Who can lift it, and can the container be secured for transport? Route Is the route open and safe in the current conditions? Care Who supports children or dependent adults during the trip? Fallback What happens if the site is closed or has no suitable water? For someone living alone or without transport, ask a trusted supporter for a specific manageable delivery. If safe supply cannot be maintained at home, consider a confirmed alternative location before running out. Relocation planning should include care, accessibility, and pets rather than focusing only on gallons. When service returns: wait for clearance and follow the reset Pressure returning is not the same as an advisory being lifted. Use the utility’s actual clearance and follow its directions for flushing, appliances, filters, ice, and any affected equipment. The correct reset depends on the incident and your plumbing; there is no universal number of minutes that certifies every home. Confirm the notice has changed for your service area, not only a neighboring area. Read the reset instructions before opening taps or restarting water-connected appliances. Follow equipment-specific guidance for filters, dispensers, and any affected private-well system. Keep restricted-use water clearly separated until it is no longer needed or has been disposed of appropriately. Replenish the stored drinking-water reserve and record what the household actually used. If water remains unusual or the situation is unclear, use the suitable alternative and seek further guidance through a safe, reachable channel. Record which supplies, labels, carrying arrangements, or contacts would make the next outage easier. Build an emergency water supply and know how your household will handle sanitation. Do not use heating-system or radiator water for drinking. Inventory clean containers and safe water, then prioritise drinking, food, medicines and hand hygiene. Do not use nonpotable water in food or formula. Plan toilet and waste arrangements separately and keep them away from food and water storage. Give one person responsibility for clean drinking-water containers and another for dirty water or sanitation. Keep containers manageable for the person who must lift them; avoid unmarked bottles accessible to young children. Water Identify the problem before using another source Keep drinking-quality water for the right tasks Calculate what you have and when you need more Handle a boil-water notice correctly Manage hygiene and toilet needs separately Resupply without turning the trip into another problem When service returns: wait for clearance and follow the reset Find the notice Check the affected address, restoration estimate and any advisory. Prioritize safe water Reserve approved water for drinking, medications, formula, food and pets. Plan hygiene Use local health instructions for sanitation and safe handwashing without running water. Wait for clearance Follow flushing and treatment instructions once the utility restores service.

title: Water purification
summary: Use safe bottled water when available. For microbial risk, bring clear water to a rolling boil for 1 minute, or 3 minutes above 6,500 feet, and cool before use. Water contaminated with fuel, chemicals or radioactive material cannot be made safe by boiling or ordinary disinfection.
text: Does clear water mean safe water? No. Clarity does not show whether germs, fuel, pesticides or other chemicals are present. Select the safest source available and identify suspected contamination before choosing treatment. Boiling or ordinary filtration does not resolve every chemical hazard. What if the label differs from an online recipe? Follow the exact treatment product instructions for the water condition, volume and contact time. Do not mix products or estimate a stronger dose. A device’s microbial claims and maintenance requirements must match the actual task.  Store treated water in clean covered containers and prevent recontamination. Clear water can still contain germs. Ordinary filters may not remove viruses or chemicals. Choose the least contaminated available source and establish whether the problem is microbial or chemical. If the source may contain fuel, industrial chemicals or radioactive material, find another source; a camping filter or boiling is not a universal solution. Keep untreated and treated water in different labeled containers. Use clean utensils and teach each person how safe water is dispensed. Plan extra care for infant feeding and people with weakened immunity; a field filter is not automatically suitable for every medical use. Water Check the source Avoid floodwater or sources suspected of toxic contamination; find an approved alternative. Clarify cloudy water Let sediment settle or strain through a clean cloth before treatment; this alone does not disinfect it. Boil for germs Use the appropriate time and cool safely in a clean container. If boiling is unavailable Use a treatment product as labeled and official guidance for your water source; filters have different capabilities.

title: When authorities are unsafe to approach
summary: If contacting an official could expose you or your family to harm, prioritise immediate physical safety and use trusted private contacts or independently verified humanitarian and local legal support when safe. Do not publish sensitive locations or confront armed personnel. Keep essential documents and a realistic shelter or relocation plan.
text: If contacting an official could expose you or your family to harm, prioritise immediate physical safety and use trusted private contacts or independently verified humanitarian and local legal support when safe. Do not publish sensitive locations or confront armed personnel. Keep essential documents and a realistic shelter or relocation plan.    Qualified local advice matters because legal protections, detention risks and available services differ. Independent support may also be unavailable; build the plan around the resources you actually have. This page cannot guarantee privacy, legal protection or safe passage. Do not record, photograph or document an incident if doing so increases immediate danger. If no safe support channel is available, keep the family together in the safest reachable place and reduce unnecessary travel and disclosure. Reassess opportunities using verified information rather than a promised rescue. Assign a trusted adult to each person who needs assistance. Keep medicines, essential contacts and a workable reunion plan with the group. Make decisions around the least mobile person, not the fastest; avoid splitting the family without a clear, safe way to reconnect. For this situation, brief every person on the first action: assess the actual threat. Agree who will manage children, pets or mobility needs while that action happens. This page cannot guarantee privacy, legal protection or safe passage. Do not record, photograph or document an incident if doing so increases immediate danger. government threat unsafe police authorities unsafe persecution safety hostile authorities Assess the actual threat Separate verified incidents and direct threats from rumours. Think about who can access your location or information and whether a call, visit or public post could increase exposure. Identify independent support Find humanitarian or local legal contacts through their own websites or a trusted existing relationship. Verify a contact through a second channel before sharing sensitive details. Limit unnecessary exposure Share your location and travel plans only with people who need them. Review location sharing and account access; do not assume an app or a private message guarantees confidentiality. Prepare essential records Keep identification, medicines, written contacts and copies of necessary documents accessible. Store backups securely without exposing other family members. Choose a practical safety plan Agree where the household can shelter, who can host you and how to reconnect if separated. Avoid confrontational actions that increase immediate danger.

title: Wildfire
summary: Check evacuation notices for your address. Leave promptly when ordered, using the current official route; do not delay for possessions. If a fire threatens your escape or you are trapped, call emergency services with your precise location.
text: When should a household with access needs leave? Arrange transport, medicine, pets and equipment before routes become crowded or smoky. Leaving early can reduce the difficulty of moving a person who needs extra time; verify the route and destination rather than relying on a single notification. Can a respirator make a road safe? No. A particle respirator does not protect against heat, every gas or a blocked road. Smoke protection is one part of the decision; active fire, access and changing wind can make travel unsafe regardless of a mask.  Return only when reentry is allowed. Check for damaged utilities, hot debris and continuing smoke. A smoke-control room cannot protect you from a fire approaching the building. Leave before the only usable route is threatened. If no official update is reachable, act on visible nearby fire, rapidly worsening conditions and verified local information rather than waiting for an order. Do not drive into smoke with unknown visibility or through flames. Assign one person to dependents and pets and another to transport and contacts. Keep essential medicine, access aids and car keys together. Agree on a reunion place that is outside the threatened area, with a second option if access changes. Fire & air Confirm your zone Use fire agency and emergency management alerts rather than old perimeter maps. Gather people and pets Take essential medicines, identification, keys and phone power without delaying departure. Use official routes Smoke and closures can change quickly; do not drive into heavy smoke or flames. Report your destination Tell an out-of-area contact where you are going and follow shelter instructions.

title: Wildfire smoke
summary: For smoke without an immediate fire threat, stay indoors with windows and doors closed, use filtered recirculated air or a portable air cleaner, and check local air-quality updates. If ordered to evacuate, leave promptly. Severe breathing difficulty requires emergency medical help.
text: Separate an approaching fire from a smoke exposure problem.  What if closing windows makes the home too hot? Smoke reduction must be balanced with safe temperature. Check a cooler location with cleaner air and the ability to meet medical or access needs. Do not keep a vulnerable person in dangerous heat simply to preserve a closed room. Can any mask filter smoke? Loose face coverings do not provide the same particle protection as a well-fitting approved respirator. Particle respirators do not remove gases and may not fit children or everyone who needs one. Reduce exposure and seek medical guidance for breathing problems.  Keep checking changing wind, fire perimeter, and air-quality conditions. People with heart or lung disease, children, older adults, and pregnant people may need added precautions or clinical advice. If fire threatens the building or officials order departure, indoor smoke control is no substitute for evacuation. If breathing becomes difficult or symptoms are severe, seek urgent medical help. Create one cleaner-air room using safe filtration if available, reduce indoor smoke sources and avoid strenuous activity. Do not overheat a sealed home; move to a safer breathable and cooler place if you cannot maintain both air quality and safe temperature. Check people with lung or heart disease, pregnancy-related needs and infants more often. Plan low-exposure activities and keep prescribed medicines accessible. A designated cleaner room must still be comfortable, reachable and usable for the people inside. Fire & air Know which problem you face Check official fire, evacuation, and air-quality notices for your address. An evacuation order changes the decision immediately. If leaving, leave early Take people, pets, medication, keys, and essentials; tell a contact where you are going. Use the evacuation guide and current route instructions. If sheltering from smoke Close windows and doors. Set HVAC to recirculate where possible, use a portable air cleaner or a cleaner indoor room, and avoid adding indoor smoke from candles, frying, or smoking. Limit outside exposure If you must go outside in smoke, a well-fitting N95 or P100 respirator can reduce particle exposure; ordinary cloth masks do not provide the same protection.

title: Winter storm
summary: Stay indoors and postpone travel during dangerous snow, ice or blowing snow. Keep heat safe, use battery lighting and watch for power loss. If stranded in a vehicle, stay with it unless a safer shelter is clearly accessible.
text: Check on people who rely on powered equipment or may lack safe heat. Arrange relocation before indoor temperatures become dangerous. Do not walk away from a stranded vehicle in poor visibility unless you know a safe nearby destination. Keep dry layers, safe food, water and battery light together. If stranded in a vehicle, keep the exhaust clear before running the engine and conserve fuel; do not sleep with the engine running. Remain with the vehicle when walking would expose you to poor visibility or severe cold. Account for children, older people, pets and anyone who needs assistance before moving. Keep shoes, medicines and a torch in the shelter area. Decide who helps whom and who carries the essential supplies; do not send a lone child to retrieve items. For this situation, brief every person on the first action: check road conditions. Agree who will manage children, pets or mobility needs while that action happens. Do not walk away from a stranded vehicle in poor visibility unless you know a safe nearby destination. Winter Check road conditions Use official closures and forecasts before deciding to travel. Keep warmth safe Wear dry layers; never heat a home with an oven, grill or indoor generator. Prepare for outages Keep essential medicines, water, food, light and charged batteries accessible. If stranded Call for help with your location. If running the engine briefly for heat, first clear snow from the exhaust and crack a window; monitor for carbon monoxide.
